title: Ownership
summary: Moves, borrows, and the fixes for E0382, in the order you reach for them.

entries.want: Let a function read a value without taking it
entries.note: Prefer `&str` over `&String`: it accepts both, and string literals too.

entries.want: Let a function modify a value without taking it
entries.code:
fn edit(s: &mut String) { s.push('!'); }
edit(&mut owned);
entries.note: Only one unique borrow at a time, and none while a shared borrow is alive.
After this, `owned` is unusable. That is the intent, not an accident.
Costs an allocation. Worth it when you mean it; a bad habit when it is a reflex.

entries.want: Return a value from a function
entries.note: Returning moves ownership out to the caller. No borrow-checker trouble.

entries.want: Check whether a type is Copy
entries.code:
// Copy: i32, f64, bool, char, &T, tuples/arrays of Copy
// Not Copy: String, Vec<T>, Box<T>, File, anything owning a resource

entries.want: Take a value out of a struct field
entries.note: Leaves `Default::default()` behind. Use `mem::replace` to choose what is left.

entries.want: Move a value into a closure
entries.note: `move` forces capture by value, which is what a thread needs.

entries.want: Share one value between many owners
entries.note: `Rc` for one thread, `Arc` across threads. Cloning an `Rc` copies a pointer, not the value.
Reading all three lines turns guessing into a decision: borrow, clone, or restructure.
